metadataReview.coordinateBasis: Forbach Tourisme publishes the Site historique des hauteurs de Spicheren through the attributed SITLOR record on Cirkwi, with explicit latitude 49.2042714 and longitude 6.9665873. These round to [6.9666,49.2043]. This is a Hauteurs sector reference point, not a surveyed troop position, exact regimental placement or centre of the entire engagement. The official tourism and municipal accounts independently establish the combat sector. No positional accuracy radius is claimed, and the visitor site is not used to locate a particular 1870 formation or to assign later memorial equipment.

equipmentIdentity.note: The municipal Spicheren monument record documents the Hohenzollern 40th Fusilier Regiment fighting there on 6 August 1870. The institutional Deutsche Biographie account of Goeben identifies the Prussian VIII Corps and its 16th Division within Steinmetz’s First Army at the same battle. These establish a Prussian infantry component within the unchanged GER 1ST ARMY(+) aggregate; this does not assert the model is the exact dress of the 40th Fusiliers. The historical polity establishes equipment eligibility only; the local participant ID, collective name and every quantity are retained.

note:
Reviewed CDB90 match 222, pinned revision e0b35ec4d798cec3bb4e6970c0f6bb7aa69e2f4c. CDB90 (CAA Database of Battles, Version 1990), tidy data maintained by Jeffrey B. Arnold. Original US Army Concepts Analysis Agency data; revised data licensed ODC-BY. Original force designations and strength interpretations are retained with each quantity. Each side is one aggregate force, including any coalition; its total is not allocated among members. Personnel casualties are not deaths. Source estimates and adjudged error margins are not statistical confidence intervals. Equipment and tactical movements are not established by this dataset. Match review: Both formations remain local. GER 1ST ARMY is not silently assigned to the post-1871 German Empire.

The Spicheren municipality identifies Frossard’s French 2nd Corps at the battle of 6 August. The Gravelotte municipality documents Palmyr Lanquetin of the 8th line infantry fighting at Spicheren; his transcribed letter is not used for its speculative enemy loss claims. The kepi, blue-grey campaign capote, garance trousers and Chassepot M1866 with sabre bayonet are a documented 1870 line-infantry analogy. Clothing, regiment, supply and branch varied; this is not a claim that every soldier of the mixed army wore or carried these items. Zouaves, tirailleurs, guards, mobiles, cavalry and artillery are not converted into line infantry. No component proportion, new participant, strength, loss or death is inferred. The Draner print used for visual corroboration was published in 1871; it is not dated to the battle and does not broaden the profile’s eligibility.

The municipal Spicheren monument record documents the Hohenzollern 40th Fusilier Regiment fighting there on 6 August 1870. The institutional Deutsche Biographie account of Goeben identifies the Prussian VIII Corps and its 16th Division within Steinmetz’s First Army at the same battle. These establish a Prussian infantry component within the unchanged GER 1ST ARMY(+) aggregate; this does not assert the model is the exact dress of the 40th Fusiliers. The leather spiked helmet, blue tunic, grey trousers and Dreyse M1862 form a representative 1870 Prussian line-infantry analogy. Helmet patterns, regimental details, clothing and equipment varied. The Auxonne helmet is a surviving November 1870 trophy, not an object proven to have been at this battle; the Carnavalet print shows several forms of dress. No fixed bayonet or precise regimental badge is reconstructed. The equipment identity Q27306 is a gate for this reviewed component only. Existing participant IDs, names, aggregate membership, all strengths, losses and deaths remain unchanged; no infantry share is inferred. Cavalry, artillery, guards, riflemen and allied states are not recategorized as this line-infantry component.
